title: Iff split of the triangle-game main theorem: Mulan can guarantee θ iff θ = 180/n for some n ≥ 2
intent: Assemble the triangle game's headline result — Mulan can force a winning angle θ from every valid triangle in finitely many steps exactly when θ = 180 / n for some integer n ≥ 2 — by splitting the biconditional with `constructor` and closing each direction with one named lemma already proved above: the necessity direction derives `∃ z, 180 = z·θ` by contradiction with `equilateral_counterexample` and converts z to a natural n ≥ 2, while the sufficiency direction rewrites θ = 180/n to 180 = n·θ and hands off to `all_win_of_divides`.

parent.name: main_theorem
parent.statement:
theorem main_theorem (θ : ℝ) (hθ0 : 0 < θ) (hθ180 : θ < 180) :
    MulanCanGuarantee θ ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n ∧ θ = 180 / n := by

children.name: equilateral_counterexample
children.statement:
theorem equilateral_counterexample (θ : ℝ) (hθ0 : 0 < θ)
    (hstar : ∀ z : ℤ, (180 : ℝ) ≠ (z : ℝ) * θ) :
    ¬ MulanCanGuarantee θ := by
children.closed_by: `exact safe_not_win θ hθ0 hstar hetri hesafe (hguar e hetri)` (line 462), after building the equilateral triangle `e = {60, 60, 60}` and proving it valid (`hetri`, lines 449-453) and safe (`hesafe`, lines 454-461)

children.name: all_win_of_divides
children.statement:
theorem all_win_of_divides (θ : ℝ) (hθ0 : 0 < θ) (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (hdvd : (180 : ℝ) = (n : ℝ) * θ) :
    ∀ s : Multiset ℝ, IsTriangle s → MulanWins θ s := by
children.closed_by: `by_cases hcaseA : ∃ v ∈ s, ∃ z : ℤ, v = (z:ℝ)*θ`; Case A hands `z.toNat` to `win_of_multiple` (line 276); Case B normalises `a, b, c` by θ, applies `interval_lemma` to pick `m` (line 306), builds a cut at `m·θ` and closes with `MulanWins.move` plus `win_of_multiple` on each child (lines 346-360)

applicability.goal_shape: A goal `P ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n ∧ θ = 180 / n` (more generally `P ↔ Q`) where the two directions are already proved as standalone lemmas: one lemma derives the right-hand side from P by contradiction against a counterexample, the other proves P from the witness n by a universal argument over all valid triangles.
applicability.use_when: both directions already exist as named lemmas whose hypotheses match the theorem's (`0 < θ`, and `θ < 180` to rule out n = 1); the theorem is a genuine iff and each side closes by a single `exact` of the corresponding lemma.
applicability.avoid_when: one direction needs a bespoke argument too large or too case-specific to be worth naming; the two lemmas are stated over different hypotheses so the hand-off needs extra rewriting; the 'iff' is really a one-way implication and one direction is trivial or empty.

claims.claim: The parent `main_theorem` closes from exactly two named project lemmas — `equilateral_counterexample` closes the necessity direction (`exact equilateral_counterexample θ hθ0 h hguar`, line 480) and `all_win_of_divides` closes the sufficiency direction (`exact all_win_of_divides θ hθ0 n hn hdvd`, line 518) — and the `constructor` on `↔` is the only glue between them.

The glue is 50 lines (the parent site, lines 469-518) while the two children carry 19 lines (`equilateral_counterexample`, 444-462) and 110 lines (`all_win_of_divides`, 251-360) between them, so 129 lines of the argument live in the named lemmas and only 50 in the iff-assembly.

Below `main_theorem` the longest chain of project lemmas is 3 deep: `main_theorem` → `equilateral_counterexample` (applies `safe_not_win`, line 462) → `safe_not_win` (applies `safe_child`, line 436) → `safe_child` (a leaf, closed by `rcases`/`linarith` on its own); a second 3-deep chain runs `main_theorem` → `all_win_of_divides` (applies `win_of_multiple`, line 276) → `win_of_multiple` (applies `triangle_with_apex`, line 121).

consequences: `constructor` on `↔` creates exactly two goals, one per direction. Necessity side: the obligation is to produce `∃ n, 2 ≤ n ∧ θ = 180/n` from `MulanCanGuarantee θ`, which the proof reduces to showing `180` is an integer multiple of θ (by contradiction with `equilateral_counterexample`) and then to excluding n = 1 via `θ < 180`. Sufficiency side: the obligation is to prove `MulanCanGuarantee θ` from `θ = 180/n`, discharged by the rewrite `180 = n·θ` plus `all_win_of_divides`. Failure modes: dropping `θ < 180` leaves n = 1 (θ = 180) unexcluded and necessity fails; if the two lemmas are not stated with matching hypotheses (`0 < θ`, `hstar` for the counterexample, `2 ≤ n` and `hdvd` for sufficiency) the `exact` hand-offs fail and the glue grows.
